grades.quote: It calls kvmmap to map each stack at the virtual address generated by KSTACK, which leaves room for the invalid stack-guard pages.
grades.reason: Says xv6 maps each kernel stack at the KSTACK address, which leaves room for invalid (unmapped) stack-guard pages. That is the kernel-stack guard-page setup. It does not explain that an overflow into the guard page causes a fault.

grades.quote: To detect a user stack overflowing the allocated stack memory, xv6 places an inaccessible guard page right below the stack by clearing the PTE_U flag. If the user stack overflows and the process tries to use an address below the stack, the hardware will generate a page-fault exception because the guard page is inaccessible to a program running in user mode.
grades.reason: Explains how an inaccessible guard page below the xv6 user stack triggers a page fault on overflow. This is the same mechanism, but it applies to the user stack, not the kernel stack the query asks about.
